scope: Official 3.1.2 carrier-materialized source build: all eleven command files, 1190 gates, 10240 full 298-bit joint shots, per-file native archive/download/purge barriers, and procedural CPU/OpenCL comparisons. The 73 exact amplitudes are separately audited in spindoctor-3.1.2-298-native-validation.json.

verification.scope: Samples the current saved procedural model's predicted state amplitudes, spin components and Born probability at actual domain addresses, then compares actual CPU and OpenCL GPU calculation arrays for that model snapshot at the end of this file. This is sampled descriptor verification, not independent certification of q.math, q.model, q.resource, circuit, or tranche answers and not a physical-RAM XOR test.

result.addressDigestEncoding: SHA-256 of completed compared addresses as big-endian unsigned 64-bit words in traversal order

sampleAssessment.modelInterpretation: At migration t=0 every address starts from alpha=1,beta=0; the shared matrix acts on that same state at every address. Address-constant predictions and exact zero components/residuals can therefore be correct.
sampleAssessment.scope: Assessment of the original native captured preview, at most32 actual compared rows. Distinct counts use exact finite nine-component vectors; ranges use finite returned components. These describe neither omitted rows nor the whole model domain. A parent summary can display fewer rows than this native capture.
sampleAssessment.countMeaning: completedSamples counts comparison operations in this job. Repeating the same descriptor, selection seed and sample request reuses the deterministic address plan; repeated job totals are not newly distinct union coverage.

result.samplePreviewAddressDigestEncoding: SHA-256 of displayed compared addresses as big-endian unsigned64-bit words in display/traversal order
result.verificationMethod: Actual RAM-resident FP64 CPU and OpenCL GPU batch arrays at distinct procedural model addresses; nine returned components plus norm and pure-spin identity checks at the stated tolerance.
result.verificationPurpose: Materialize selected addresses of the captured virtual procedural model on CPU and GPU, show what that model predicts, and check agreement and mathematical state identities at the returned tolerance.
result.predictionMeaning: Displayed amplitudes, X/Y/Z spin expectations and probabilityOne are the captured model's numerical predictions. probabilityOne is a Born probability, not an observed shot frequency. CPU/GPU agreement checks two implementations under the same model assumptions; it is not experimental or physical quantum-hardware validation, proof of unsampled addresses, or verification of unrelated calculator operands/results.
result.samplePreviewScope: First at most32 actually compared addresses, copied from completed CPU/GPU batch arrays. Omitted success rows remain counted and represented by the address digest; no sample rows are synthesized. This verifies the captured procedural descriptor, not unrelated q.math operands/results or arbitrary physical RAM contents.
result.selectionRule: One unbiased SHA-256 offset per evenly partitioned stratum excluding boundary addresses, followed by unique deterministic boundaries; fully blocked strata are skipped.
result.scope: Completed CPU/GPU amplitude, relative-phase, norm, Born P1 and spin comparisons for the captured procedural descriptor. Partial/cancelled work is counted exactly; a bounded sample preview is retained, and no represented gate credit is issued. This is not verification of unrelated calculator results or a scan of arbitrary physical RAM.
result.previewScope: Parent metadata shows at most four actual sample rows. Complete up-to-32-row evidence is retained in the child verification JSON identified by evidenceFile/evidenceSha256.
